description: Synthetic plumbing fixture for scripts/eval_semantic_retrieval.py: authored scheduler-domain lessons and queries, most phrased without the lesson's own words. It checks that every arm runs end to end; it is too small and too artificial to measure retrieval quality.

memories.claim: Job cancellation must set JobState::Cancelled and remove the job from the queue; the legacy Aborted state is non-terminal and abort_job is not a cancellation path
Scheduler drain() only pops jobs that are already due - it is not a full sweep; evacuate() is the stable-order full sweep for snapshots and shutdown
Every dedupe-key lookup, removal, and comparison must normalize through DedupeKey::new first; raw string comparison misses case and whitespace variants
Every new serde config or persistence field must carry serde(default) with the documented default; legacy files without the field must keep parsing byte-identically
The attempts counter already includes the just-failed run; retry backoff and budget checks must use attempts-1 or they are off by one
All millisecond-to-tick conversions must round up via ticks_for_ms; plain integer division silently schedules work one tick early
Release worker reservations when abort cleanup runs, or pool capacity leaks until restart
Rotate archived log files weekly and keep eight generations
Database migrations are append-only: never edit a migration file that has already been applied
HTTP clients for local model servers must refuse redirects and ignore proxy environment variables

cases.query: Fix the off-by-one in retry backoff attempts
A job that keeps failing is given one fewer chance than its budget promises
Ticket: deadline handling must round up. A job deadline given in milliseconds is converted to scheduler ticks; partial ticks must give the job breathing room rather than cutting it short.
Timers fire slightly before the requested delay has elapsed

Ticket: snapshots must include future jobs. Persisted snapshots currently lose jobs scheduled past the capture instant; the snapshot writer must sweep every queued job, not only the currently due ones.
Saved state is missing work that was planned for later
Stopping a queued job leaves it stuck in a state that never finishes
Looking a job up by its key fails when the caller uses different capitalization
Older saved settings files stopped loading after we added a new option
Pool capacity shrinks every time a task is killed halfway
Can I correct a typo in a schema change script that already shipped?
Our embedding client followed a 302 to another host
Configure the office printer duplex default
